why: The old pattern accepted ELEVEN DIGITS IN A ROW with no punctuation at all, as long as there was a `9` in the third position — and a product EAN-13 barcode matches that. Acceptable in a heuristic that only informs; unacceptable in a rule that fails a merge, and the rule has just become deterministic. Both sides have the SAME EAN-13: the `fail` side adds the same number written WITH a Brazilian phone marker, country code 55. Whoever loosens the pattern back makes the `pass` side go red, accusing a barcode of being a phone number.
